comments.quote_zh: 我真心推荐 WIRED 的 Future Cities 纪录片，讲深圳和驻扎在那里的公司。
comments.text_zh: 我太期待某种自上而下的压力来逼 IoT 开发者认真对待安全问题了。这个行当被推到了超速运转的状态，原因是竞争激烈到疯狂：你要么把研发压缩到最短的玩命周期里，要么就眼睁睁看着自己的成果还在工作台上时，就被别的公司拿去、以你预算能承受的一半价格卖出去。[1] 过去一年，我以个人副业的身份跟深圳的硬件加速器走得很近，我从没见过哪个群体被如此逼着尽快出货，而安全只是随口一提的事后想法。想大致体会那是什么感觉，我真心推荐 WIRED 的 Future Cities 纪录片，讲深圳和驻扎在那里的公司。[2] 他们为了转瞬即逝的市场份额而挣扎，这在整个过去几年接管嵌入式硬件的社群里是普遍现象。最可悲的是，这种市场竞争并没有让消费者受益。IoT 设备从工厂出来时工程设计粗糙、维护期短得可怜，而且正如这次攻击让我们看到的，还被当作网络入侵和分布式审查的载体。就连 arduino 创始人 Massimo Banzi 广受赞誉的 IoT Manifesto[3]，也没能就开发者有责任在设备里内置一定程度的安全性给出任何全面的表述。它根本就不是那种快速随性文化的一部分
comments.text: I cannot wait for some type of top-down pressure to force IoT developers to take security seriously. The movement has been pushed into overdrive thanks to insane levels of competition where you either crush your R&D into the smallest breakneck period or you live to see your creation being sold for half of what your budget can allow by other firms lifting your efforts while you're still at the workbench.[1] I've been getting cozy with Shenzhen-based hardware accelerators for the past year as part of a personal side-venture and I have not seen a group so pressured to deliver a product as fast as possible with security being a casual afterthought. To get a decent taste of what it's like, I wholeheartedly recommend WIRED's Future Cities documentary on Shenzhen and the companies that dwell there.[2] Their struggles for ephemeral market-share are endemic of the entire community that's taken over embedded hardware for the past few years. The saddest aspect of it all is that this market competition isn't benefiting the consumer. IoT devices are coming out of the factories poorly engineered, badly maintained for far too short of a time, and as we've learned from this attack, being used as vectors for network intrusion and distributed censorship. Even arduino founder Massimo Banzi's widely-lauded IoT Manifesto[3] fails to approach any comprehensive statement regarding a dev's responsibility to build in some level of security to their devices. comments.why_zh: 展示了深圳的创客心态如何渗透到买家，以及 Hoverboard 热潮是如何兴起的。
comments.quote_zh: 作为配套材料，我强烈推荐 Wired 这部长达一小时的关于深圳的视频。值得你花时间看
comments.text_zh: 作为配套材料，我强烈推荐 Wired 这部长达一小时的关于深圳的视频。值得你花时间看：[VIDEO] 让我印象深刻的是，创客心态如此普遍且充满竞争，以至于已经渗透到了买家身上。于是有人为手机拼凑出某个新小玩意儿并开始售卖。其他人看到它卖得好就照抄，但会做些改动。购物者第一次看到它，决定想要一个带紫色挂带的，于是就到处逛，直到找到它，或者找到愿意按这个要求做的人。Hoverboard 热潮就是在这里冒起来的，同时也是它如何以及为何“熄灭”的。我觉得这是一个非常迷人的技术、创造力和经济学的试验场。
comments.text: For a companion piece I highly recommend this hour long vid by Wired about Shenzhen. It's worth your time: [VIDEO] Things that stood out to me was the maker mindset was so prevalent and competitve that it had filtered down to the buyers. So someone cobbles together some new widget for their phone and starts to sell it. Other people see it selling a nd copy it, but they make modifications. Shoppers see it for the first time and decide they want one with a purple strap, so they shop around until they find it or find someone who will make it that way. This is where the hoverboard fad bubbled up but also how and why it "flamed" out. I think it's a fascinating testbed for technology and creativity and economics.

comments.author: nexus6mike
comments.story_title: Shenzhen’s economy under strain: blame the trade war?
comments.quote_zh: 还有一部关于深圳的精彩 Wired 纪录片
comments.text_zh: 短期需求似乎正在转向越南。这似乎让各方对中国和关税采取了“观望”态度。不过，我会质疑越南是否有足够的长期制造能力 [1] [2] [3] 来维持它目前似乎享有的短期优势。如今，全球 50 个最繁忙的港口中，中国占了 16 个，包括排名第三的深圳（均按 2018 年 TEU 吞吐量计算）[4]。然而，这与其说反映的是产能，不如说反映的是当前需求／吞吐量。两国都可以从建设更多深水港中受益。中国目前有两个巴拿马型港口，第三个正在建设中。越南一个都没有，正在建第一个。相比之下，据我统计，美国有 42 个。[5] 另外，还有一部关于深圳的精彩 Wired 纪录片：[VIDEO] 。[1] [LINK] [2] www.scmp.com/economy/china-economy/article/3018403/chinese-manufacturers-returning-home-inefficient-vietnam [3] [LINK] [4] [LINK] [5] [LINK]
comments.text: Short-term demand seems to be shifting to Vietnam. This seems to have enabled a 'wait and see' approach re: China + tariffs. However, I'd question if Vietnam has enough long-term manufacturing capacity [1] [2] [3] to sustain the short-term advantage it seems to be currently enjoying. Today, China has 16 of the world's 50 busiest ports, including Shenzhen at #3 (all as measured by 2018 TEU volume). [4] However, this is less indicative of capacity than it is of current demand / throughput. Both countries could benefit from building more deep-water ports. China currently has two Panamax ports, with a third on the way. Vietnam has none and is building its first. The U.S., by comparison, has 42 by my count. [5] Separately, there's a great Wired documentary on Shenzhen: [VIDEO] . comments.text_zh: 问题是，没人会来给你解释中国到底在发生什么。理解中国的生态需要投入相当大的精力，而真正懂的人宁愿跟圈内人聊，也不愿对着一堵墙说话。其实我写这些的时候都有点难为情。如果你愿意认为 PayPal、eBay 和它们现代的中国版本之间没有区别，那随你。但在你真正在中国用过这些东西（或者至少有足够的想象力）之前，你其实并不知道那里是不是真有什么东西。[LINK] [VIDEO] [LINK]
comments.text: The thing is that no one is going to explain to you what's going on in China. Understanding the Chinese ecosystem takes considerable effort and the people that do understand would rather talk to others in the know than to a wall. I actually cringe a bit even writing this. If you want to think that there's no difference between PayPal, eBay and modern Chinese versions you are free to do so. But until you've used these things in China (or at least had sufficient imagination), you won't actually know if there is something there. [LINK] [VIDEO] [LINK]

comments.author: freeflight
comments.story_title: As China Hacked, U.S. Businesses Turned a Blind Eye
comments.text_zh: 特别奇怪的是，大家都觉得特朗普因为恨中国而显得古怪，但如今这么多人只是重复那些通常完全毫无根据的反华 FUD。不管是所谓华为监视所有人，还是中国政府往 Super Micro 主板上植入芯片，再荒谬的东西都能被传播，而且传播者偏偏就是五眼联盟自己。中国搞黑客攻击吗？当然搞，美国也搞，甚至从盟友那里窃取知识产权。但我严重怀疑这造成的损失能达到 570 亿美元，那只是一个类似盗版损失那样的虚高数字。现实中，许多有趣的创新，尤其是在硬件层面，已经在中国发生了很多年。他们将在规模上超过美国的创客运动 [0]。[0] [VIDEO]
comments.text: It's super weird how everybody considered Trump odd for his hate for China, yet these days so many people just repeat the, usually completely baseless, anti-China FUD. Whether it's Huawei supposedly spying on everybody or the Chinese government putting implants on Super Micro boards, nothing is too absurd to be spread by, out of all parties, Five eyes themselves. Does China hack? Of course, so does the US, it even steals IP from allies. But I seriously doubt the damages for that go into the $57 billion, that's just a piracy-damages like inflated number. In reality, a whole lot of interesting innovation, particularly on the hardware level, has already been happening in China for years already. They gonna out-make the US maker movement, on a massive scale [0]. [0] [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: 中国用于科学研究的经费将在 2019 年达到 GDP 的 2.5%：[LINK] WIRED UK 在 2016 年制作的一部纪录片解释了许多文化和法律方面的原因：[VIDEO] 中国有一些硬件产业，其运作方式类似于开源软件的运作方式。一篇关于专利到期对 3D 打印影响的文章（2013）：[LINK] 每天 90 分钟、到晚上 10 点：中国为年轻游戏玩家制定规则：[LINK] 许多亚洲国家已经针对数字成瘾采取了有力措施（我敢打赌，这将是新冠之后要解决的下一个重要问题）。中国的可持续城市交通革命：[LINK] [LINK] > 总体而言，巴西、中国、印度、印度尼西亚、肯尼亚、墨西哥、尼日利亚和俄罗斯 12 至 24 岁的人群中，有 79% 表示他们对世界的发展方向感到乐观；相比之下，在澳大利亚、法国、德国、英国和瑞典等富裕得多的地方，这一比例只有约一半。在美国，这个数字是 63%。[LINK] > 在我们调查的排名靠前的国家中，中国的开发者最乐观，他们相信今天出生的人会比父母过上更好的生活。法国和德国等西欧国家的开发者则属于对未来最不乐观的群体。[LINK] 中国也比美国大得多。它的人口是美国的 3 倍。这些人终将在某个时候与西方人达到同等水平。有太多有趣的事情值得讨论和质疑。
comments.text: China’s funding for science and research to reach 2.5 per cent of GDP in 2019: [LINK] A documentary by WIRED UK done in 2016 explains many cultural and legal reasons: [VIDEO] China has hardware industries that work similar to how open source software works. An article on effects of expiring patents on 3D printing (2013): [LINK] 90 Minutes a Day, Until 10 P.M.: China Sets Rules for Young Gamers: [LINK] Many Asian countries have already taken strong steps for digital addiction (which will be the next important problem to tackle after covid, I bet). China’s sustainable urban transport revolution: [LINK] [LINK] > Overall, 79% of people between the ages of 12 and 24 in Brazil, China, India, Indonesia, Kenya, Mexico, Nigeria, and Russia say they feel optimistic about the direction of the world, compared to only about half of those in far more well-off places like Australia, France, Germany, Great Britain, and Sweden. In the United States, the number is 63%. [LINK] > Of the top countries on our survey, China has developers that are the most optimistic, believing that people born today will have a better life than their parents. Developers in Western European countries like France and Germany are among the least optimistic about the future. [LINK] China is also much larger country than US. It has 3x more people than US. Those individuals are going to be at par with people in west at some point. There are so many interesting things to discuss and question.

comments.why_zh: 考察深圳的仿制制造生态系统，以及世界能从中学习什么。
comments.text_zh: Bunnie Huang [1] 就这个话题写过/讲过。我想他在 Shenzen 那部纪录片 [2] 里提到过。纪录片页面上的引文：> 我们考察了已经出现的独特制造生态系统，得以接触世界领先的硬件原型制作文化，同时挑战来自西方的误解。这部影片探讨了“山寨”——或者说仿制制造——的演变如何改变了传统的商业、分销和创新模式，并追问世界其他地方能从这座所谓的“硬件硅谷”中学到什么。1: [LINK] 2: [VIDEO]
comments.text: Bunnie Huang [1] has written/spoke on this topic. I think he mentions it in the Shenzen documentary [2]. Quote from the documentary page: > We examine the unique manufacturing ecosystem that has emerged, gaining access to the world’s leading hardware-prototyping culture whilst challenging misconceptions from the west. The film looks at how the evolution of “Shanzhai” – or copycat manufacturing – has transformed traditional models of business, distribution and innovation, and asks what the rest of the world can learn from this so-called “Silicon Valley of hardware". 1: [LINK] 2: [VIDEO]
